title: Max Sum of Rectangle No Larger Than K
summary: Given an m x n matrix and an integer k, find the maximum sum of any rectangle within the matrix whose sum does not exceed k.
statement: Given an m x n matrix and an integer k, find the maximum sum of any rectangle within the matrix whose sum does not exceed k. Ensure such a rectangle exists.
constraints: The matrix has 1 to 100 rows and columns; -100 <= each value <= 100; -100000 <= k <= 100000.
Return the largest sum <= k over nonempty axis-aligned contiguous rectangles. At least one feasible rectangle is guaranteed.
reference_solution:
def max_bounded_rectangle(matrix, k):
    from bisect import bisect_left
    rows, cols = len(matrix),len(matrix[0])
    transpose = rows > cols
    narrow, wide = min(rows,cols),max(rows,cols)
    best = None
    for top in range(narrow):
        sums = [0]*wide
        for bottom in range(top,narrow):
            prefixes = [0]
            for c in range(wide):
                sums[c] += matrix[c][bottom] if transpose else matrix[bottom][c]
                prefixes.append(prefixes[-1]+sums[c])
            coordinates = sorted(set(prefixes))
            size = len(coordinates)
            ranks = {value:i+1 for i,value in enumerate(coordinates)}
            counts = [0]*(size+1)
            seen = 0
            step = 1 << (size.bit_length()-1)
            for current in prefixes:
                index = bisect_left(coordinates,current-k)
                less = 0
                while index:
                    less += counts[index]
                    index -= index & -index
                if less < seen:
                    # Select the (less+1)-th previously inserted prefix.
                    rank, index, bit = less+1,0,step
                    while bit:
                        nxt = index+bit
                        if nxt <= size and counts[nxt] < rank:
                            rank -= counts[nxt]
                            index = nxt
                        bit >>= 1
                    candidate = current-coordinates[index]
                    best = candidate if best is None else max(best,candidate)
                    if best == k:
                        return best
                index = ranks[current]
                while index <= size:
                    counts[index] += 1
                    index += index & -index
                seen += 1
    return best

def max_bounded_rectangle(matrix, k):
    return max((sum(row[left:right]) for row in matrix for left in range(len(row)) for right in range(left+1,len(row)+1) if sum(row[left:right]) <= k),default=0)
hints: Fixing two boundaries compresses the rectangle problem into a bounded subarray-sum problem.
For current prefix p, find the smallest earlier prefix >= p-k. Use ordered counts of compressed prefix values.
Enumerate bands along the shorter dimension. Maintain a Fenwick tree of earlier prefix counts and select the first eligible prefix rank.
Earlier prefix q gives sum p-q. Choosing the least q >= p-k maximizes the feasible sum, and every rectangle appears in one band.
editorial: Enumerate top/bottom boundaries along the shorter matrix dimension without copying a transpose. Compress each band into column sums and prefix sums. Coordinate compression plus a Fenwick count tree supplies predecessor-count and rank-selection operations, finding the smallest earlier prefix at least p-k in logarithmic time. Query before inserting p so only nonempty subarrays count. The oracle independently sums every cell of every small rectangle.

tests.explanation: Rows 0..1 and columns 1..2 contain [[0,1],[-2,3]], summing to 2. No permitted answer can exceed the bound 2.
All three cells sum to 3. A sliding window for positive values would miss how the negative cell makes the larger rectangle feasible.
